overall_summary: Space-themed 'What If' scenarios and extreme planetary physics are the clear drivers of engagement and views for FACTVERSE, consistently hitting 800-1,000+ views. Conversely, psychology and brain facts are severely underperforming, rarely breaking 100 views. Longer Shorts (19-21s) perform significantly better than shorter 12-16s clips, likely due to better pacing and deeper narrative immersion.

winning_patterns.pattern: First-person 'What If You Fell Into...' space scenarios
winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,025 views, 38 likes) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (970 views, 18 likes) are among the top-performing videos.
winning_patterns.action: Establish 'What If You Fell Into...' as a weekly recurring series, focusing on the most hostile environments in the known universe.

winning_patterns.pattern: Extreme planetary weather and composition facts
winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1,025 views, 36 likes) and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (721 views, 25 likes) show high viewer retention and engagement.
winning_patterns.action: Create visually striking videos highlighting bizarre cosmic weather patterns, using highly descriptive, sensory-rich titles.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (5-10 views) and 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' (17 views) consistently fail to gain traction.
weak_patterns.action: Pivot away from generic psychology/brain facts, or reframe them entirely under a high-stakes mystery or survival lens.

weak_patterns.pattern: Ultra-short duration (12-16 seconds) generic biology facts
weak_patterns.evidence: 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' (118 views at 12s, compared to 363 views when extended to 21s) and 'The Only Animal That Can Live Forever' (69 views, 16s) underperform.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid rushing complex facts into under-16-second formats. Standardize on a 19-21 second duration to allow for a proper narrative arc.

next_video.concept: What If You Fell Into WASP-76b (The Planet of Liquid Iron Rain)?
next_video.opening_direction: If you fell into WASP-76b, you wouldn't just burn—you'd be shredded by sideways-falling molten iron rain.
next_video.twist_direction: Explain how the extreme 4,300°F day-side temperatures vaporize metal, which then condenses and falls as liquid iron on the cooler night side.
next_video.reason: Leverages the highly successful 'What If' space survival format, utilizes the optimal 21-second duration, and targets the peak engagement window observed in top-performing uploads.

experiment: Test the 'What If' framing on a deep-sea oceanography topic (e.g., 'What If You Fell Into the Mariana Trench?') to determine if the format's success is tied strictly to space or if it translates to other high-curiosity extreme environments.
